map.Berg平衡量表(BBS)14项测试，每项0-4分，总分56分，评估静态和动态平: Berg Balance Scale (BBS) with 14 items, 0-4 points each, 56 points total, assessing static and dynamic balance ability.
map.Berg 平衡量表共 14 项（坐起、独立站立、独立坐、坐下、转移、闭眼站立、双: The Berg Balance Scale has 14 items (sit-to-stand, unsupported standing, unsupported sitting, sitting to standing, transfer, standing with eyes closed, feet together, reaching forward, picking an object from the floor, turning around to look behind, turning 360 degrees in place, stepping onto a stool, standing with one foot in front of the other, standing on one leg), each 0 to 4 points, total 0 to 56 points; 45 points or above means low fall risk, 40 to 44 means moderate risk, below 40 means high risk (assistive devices and supervision recommended); a single item scoring 4 means independent completion, 0 means unable to complete.
map.请完成各项测试评分后查看结果: Please complete the item scores to view results
map.BBS ≤ 45分提示有跌倒风险；每降低1分，跌倒风险增加约6-8%。该量表广泛: BBS ≤45 points indicates fall risk; for every 1-point decrease the fall risk rises by about 6-8%. This scale is widely used in stroke, Parkinson disease, and geriatric rehabilitation assessment.
map.14 项×0-4 合计 48/56，属低风险（>44）；若<45 跌倒风险=(4: 14 items × 0-4 sum to 48/56, which is low risk (>44); if <45 the fall risk = (45 - total) × 7%, e.g. a score of 40 gives a risk of about 35.
map.合计 20 分（≤20 红区），平衡严重受损，需辅助下活动并防跌，建议坐位平衡与: Summing to 20 points (≤20 red zone), balance is severely impaired; activity requires assistance and fall prevention, and sitting balance plus transfer training is advised.
map.≤20 跌倒高危、21-40 中危、41-44 低危、45-52 正常、53-5: ≤20 high fall risk, 21-40 moderate risk, 41-44 low risk, 45-52 normal, 53-56 excellent; below 45 fall prevention should be implemented.
map.Berg 总分 56，临床上 0–20 分提示需轮椅、21–40 分辅助下行走、: Berg totals 56; clinically 0-20 points suggests wheelchair use, 21-40 walking with assistance, 41-56 independent walking. But a more critical criterion is that a change of 8 points or more is needed to exceed measurement error and count as real functional change. Another point: Berg is sensitive to static balance but has limited discrimination for dynamic reactive balance (the response to being pushed), so high-risk fallers should also cross-validate with the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test.
